cmds.narrate:
Beneath every city in Asterreach, a buried bell keeps the seasons.

Tonight, Bellweather lights its lanterns for the toll.

cmds.text: There you are! Rowan Vale, courier of the year, missing on the one night the whole city wants a parcel.
I was helping Mrs. Abernethy carry lanterns. She tips in biscuits.
Hale's been shouting your name across Lantern Square. Something sealed for the Bell Station. Urgent, she says. She says that about everything.
Oh — and Wren went up to the station early. Said she'd catch you at the Lantern Bridge after the toll.
She's working on festival night?
Your sister's always working. Go on. Post Office is east, on the square. I'm helping at my uncle's stall till the toll.

cmds.tutorial: Move with the left stick, D-pad, WASD or arrow keys (or drag on the left of a touchscreen). Talk and examine with A / Enter / Space. Hold B / Shift to run.
cmds.title: Getting around

ev_opening.recap: Nessa told Rowan that Postmistress Hale needs an urgent delivery taken to the Bell Station, and that Wren will meet Rowan at the Lantern Bridge after the toll.

then.text: A sealed Authority parcel on Lanternwake? Somebody important forgot something. Or wants it delivered by someone nobody notices.
Hey. After the toll, come find me. I… have a thing I want to tell you. Nothing bad. Probably.

else.text: Post Office. East. Lantern Square. Hale. Go!

cmds.text: Rowan Vale! Finally. You know how many couriers are drunk on cider tonight? All of them but you.
Sealed parcel, Authority stamp. A calibration fork for engineer Mira Fen at the Bell Station. It must be there before the toll.
It's humming.
Forks do that. Don't drop it, don't open it, don't sing near it. Station's north through the square.

cmds.tutorial: Open the menu with Y / Tab / the MENU button to check your party, items, equipment and the Journal. The Journal (View / J) always shows your current objective and a recap.
cmds.title: Menu & Journal

ev_hale_delivery.recap: Hale gave Rowan a sealed Authority tuning fork to deliver to engineer Mira Fen.

cmds.text: Station's north through the square, Rowan. Before the toll!

then.narrate: Mrs. Abernethy's door. Through the window, two teacups on the table — she always set one for Wren.

else.narrate: Mrs. Abernethy's house. She's out on the street tonight.

cmds.text: Rowan, dear! Tell your sister I saved her a honey biscuit. She works too hard. You both do.
The toll keeps the floods out of the lower wards, you know. Last spring my cellar stayed dry for the first time in forty years.
Two years running, no famine in the river towns. Say what you like about the Authority — they keep the seasons honest.
My boy's lantern is the green one, third from the bridge. He painted a fish on it. It looks like a potato.
Night crew's already below in the core. Tamsin, Joss, and Pell drew the short straws. Festival shift.
Move along, citizen. The ceremony is in the square. Couriers to the platform.

then.narrate: Sealed with Authority chain and wax.

else.narrate: The great brass doors. Engineers only past this point.

cmds.narrate: A ceremonial replica of the buried bell. Its rim is engraved with the names of every season it has kept.

cmds.text: There's my little courier. You walked the whole way without a single shortcut? I'm impressed.
Wren! What are you doing up here? Nessa said you were working.
Checking numbers. Pitch logs, mostly. Someone's been adjusting them, and the adjustments don't add up.

do.text: Small changes. A quarter-tone here, a quarter-tone there. Small enough that nobody asks. That's what bothers me.
I will. After the toll. I promise. You can buy me a honey cake with your enormous courier wages.

cmds.text: Meet me at the Lantern Bridge after the toll. I want to show you something.
And Rowan — whatever happens tonight, don't let anyone tell you what you remember.
That's ominous.
That's sisterly. Go on, your engineer's waiting.

ev_wren.recap: Rowan met Wren at the station. She has been investigating altered pitch logs and asked Rowan to meet at the Lantern Bridge after the toll: "Don't let anyone tell you what you remember."

cmds.text: Bridge. After the toll. And deliver your parcel before Hale has a heart attack.

then.text: If you're a courier, you're early. If you're a tourist, the ceremony's in the square.

else.text: A courier with an Authority seal. That'll be my calibration fork. Thank you—
It's been humming since I picked it up.
It's flat. A quarter-tone flat. If I calibrate the resonators to this, the toll won't just draw from the bell. It'll pull wider. Into the street.
I designed those resonators. I know what they do when they're tuned wrong.
Engineer Fen. Is there a difficulty with my fork?
Adjunct Sallow. The pitch is wrong. I'm not installing it.
Then the station will toll on its existing settings, which I approved this morning. The flood wards will hold. The orchards will eat. The city will thank us.
Courier. Your delivery is complete. Enjoy the festival.
…Keep the fork. Take it back to Hale. If anyone asks, it was refused at the platform.
And if anything feels wrong at the toll — anything — find me afterwards.

ev_mira_delivery.recap: Mira found the fork tuned a quarter-tone flat and refused to install it. Adjunct Sallow overruled her: the toll will proceed on settings he approved. Mira told Rowan to keep the fork.

cmds.text: The toll's starting soon in the square. Go. I'll be watching the gauges.

cmds.narrate: Lantern Square fills with people. Lanterns rise. Somewhere below the cobbles, the great bell waits.

cmds.text: Citizens of Bellweather! For eleven years, the toll has kept the floods from the lower wards and bread on every table along the Rainward Line.
Tonight we draw a little of the old season's memory from the bell, and in exchange, it keeps us safe. A small price. A fair one.
Toll! Toll! Toll!
…That's not the right note.
My arm— the scar's burning—!

cmds.narrate:
…

When Rowan opens their eyes, the lanterns are still burning.

The tuning fork in their satchel is humming, warm as a held hand.

cmds.text: Everyone's… fine? They're just standing there.
Wren. The bridge. She said the bridge.

ev_toll.recap: During the Lanternwake toll, the bell rang a wrong note. Rowan's old scar burned and the tuning fork hummed. Afterwards, the crowd seemed dazed but unhurt. Wren had asked to meet at the Lantern Bridge.

cmds.text: Station's sealed by order of Adjunct Sallow. Maintenance incident. Go home, citizen.
Nobody in or out. That includes couriers.
Wren? …Wren!

cmds.narrate: The Lantern Bridge is crowded with people looking at the water, puzzled, as if they'd come here for a reason they can't name.
A red scarf is knotted to the railing. Neat, careful knots. Wren's knots.

cmds.text: She was here. She left this for me — she wouldn't just leave it.
Someone must have seen her. Mrs. Abernethy. Hale. Anyone.

ev_bridge_after_toll.recap: Wren wasn't at the bridge. Rowan found her red scarf tied to the railing.

then.text: Are you feeling all right, dear? You look pale. Come for biscuits later.

else.text: Mrs. Abernethy, have you seen Wren? She was meant to meet me—
Wren, dear? I don't know a Wren. Is she one of the new couriers?
My sister. Wren Vale. You taught her to knit. You save her honey biscuits every festival!
Oh, Rowan. Your parents only ever had the one child. You. I'd remember, sweetheart — I was at the naming.
Is it the toll? Some folk come over strange. Sit down, have some water.

cmds.text: Odd night. I came out here to meet someone and I can't think who. Must've been the cider.
Wren? No… no, I don't think so. Is she the one who fixed the Hollins' gutter? No, that was a man. Wasn't it?
Rowan! Look, I drew the kite lady. She fixed my kite last week. Nobody remembers her but I do. Well — mostly I do.

cmds.narrate: A crayon drawing: a tall woman in a red scarf, holding a kite with a lightning bolt on it. Underneath, in careful letters: WREN.

cmds.text: Pim… can I borrow this? It's really important.
You can keep it if you find her. And — here. She gave me this string. You can have it too. For luck.

ev_pim_drawing.recap: Pim, a child, still half-remembers Wren and gave Rowan a drawing of her.

cmds.text: Hale. Wren Vale. She's a courier here. She's been a courier here for six years.
Rowan, I've run this office for twenty. I know every courier on my books, and I've never heard that name.
…But you're shaking. Fine. The night ledgers are on the back shelf. Look for yourself.
Get some rest, Rowan. The toll does strange things. My own head's been foggy all night.

then.narrate: The night ledgers. Hale is watching — better ask her first.

else.narrate: The courier ledger for last week. Page after page in Hale's cramped hand…
…and one page in a different hand. Slanted, quick, familiar. Deliveries to the Records Hall and the Bell Station, signed W. Vale. Countersigned by Hale.

else.text: That's my signature. I— I don't remember signing that.
That's Wren's handwriting. She was here.

cmds.narrate: Parcels waiting for owners. Some of the labels have been smudged, as if someone wiped a name off.

then.text: The scarf. The ledger. Pim's drawing. She existed. She exists. They didn't just forget her — someone made them forget.
I need to go home and think.

then.narrate: Wren's bed, made with hospital corners. Her books on the shelf. Her boots by the door.
The whole street insists this room only ever had one bed.

else.narrate: Wren's bed, neatly made. A stack of pitch-log copies sits on the pillow. She brings work home.

cmds.narrate: Two mugs, one with a chipped handle. Wren always takes the chipped one. "Character," she says.
Wren's notebooks. Lists of dates and numbers, pitch values in neat columns. One column is circled three times: WICK — 432 -> 426.

Records Hall — closed for Lanternwake.

A fresh Authority notice: "Memory disturbances following the toll are temporary and harmless. Report persistent symptoms to your ward warden."

North: Bell Station.  West: Wick Street & the canal.
Post Office — Records Hall — The Copper Kettle (rooms, food, the Hall of Paths)

then.narrate: The ceremonial bell is silent. Rowan's scar prickles when they come close to it.

party_say.text: The real bell is sixty feet under us. This one's for show. I used to think that was charming.

fallback.text: It rang wrong. I heard it ring wrong.

else.narrate: A replica of the buried bell, garlanded for Lanternwake.

cmds.text: The toll's the best part. You feel it in your teeth. Then everything's calm for a whole season.
I felt it in my teeth, all right. And now there's a word on the tip of my tongue and I can't reach it.
My cousin in Glass Orchard says the toll is why the harvest never fails anymore. Whole villages that used to starve.
There were more of us on this street yesterday. I'm sure of it. Aren't I?
Eleven tolls I've seen. The Authority always says it's harmless. I keep a diary, just in case.
I checked my diary just now. Three pages are about someone called 'W.' I've no idea who that is. My handwriting, though.
I'm going to fly my kite during the toll! The kite lady fixed it. It's got a lightning bolt.
Festival's outside, courier. I'm not festive.
The big fellow at the bar used to be a warden captain. They took his badge after some business in Glass Orchard. Nobody says what.
Marta says the rooms are cheap tonight. Half the city forgot they booked them.
Welcome to the Copper Kettle. A bed's 40 crowns — that restores your strength, and you can write in the ledger (save) after.
